original_value: Address event representation (AER) cameras have recently attracted more attention due to the advantages of high temporal resolution and low power consumption, compared with traditional frame-based cameras. Since AER cameras record the visual input as asynchronous discrete events, they are inherently suitable to coordinate with the spiking neural network (SNN), which is biologically plausible and energy-efficient on neuromorphic hardware. However, using SNN to perform the AER object classification is still challenging, due to the lack of effective learning algorithms for this new representation. To tackle this issue, we propose an AER object classification model using a novel segmented probability-maximization (SPA) learning algorithm. Technically, 1) the SPA learning algorithm iteratively maximizes the probability of the classes that samples belong to, in order to improve the reliability of neuron responses and effectiveness of learning; 2) a peak detection (PD) mechanism is introduced in SPA to locate informative time points segment by segment, based on which information within the whole event stream can be fully utilized by the learning. Extensive experimental results show that, compared to state-of-the-art methods, not only our model is more effective, but also it requires less information to reach a certain level of accuracy.

result.paraphrase: Address event representation (AER) cameras have recently drawn increased attention because, compared with traditional frame-based cameras, they offer high temporal resolution and low power consumption. Since AER cameras encode visual input as asynchronous discrete events, they are naturally suited to work with spiking neural networks (SNNs), which are biologically plausible and energy-efficient on neuromorphic hardware. However, AER object classification with SNNs remains challenging because effective learning algorithms for this new representation are still lacking. To address this problem, we propose an AER object classification model based on a novel segmented probability-maximization (SPA) learning algorithm. Specifically, 1) SPA iteratively maximizes the probability of the classes to which samples belong, improving the reliability of neuron responses and the effectiveness of learning; 2) SPA incorporates a peak detection (PD) mechanism to identify informative time points segment by segment, enabling full use of information across the entire event stream. Extensive experiments show that, compared with state-of-the-art methods, our model is not only more effective but also requires less information to achieve a given level of accuracy.
